title: Slit-scan time ribbon
blurb: A 64-layer WebGL 2 TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY ring buffer that warps live typing, scrolling and CSS animation across space and time in one ElementGL canvas, with zero open ElementImage snapshots and no CPU readback.
question: Can a WebGL 2 TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY ring buffer warp live scrolling, typing and animating HTML across 64 frames of history with zero open ElementImage snapshots and no CPU readback, avoiding the GPU snapshot memory ceiling hit by captureElementImage() timelines?
result: Measured in headless Chrome 160 Canary (2026-11-27): 4/4 live checks pass (1.30 MP, 10 MB canvas on 412 px DPR 2.625, openSnapshots 0). Raising the desktop ring cap to 1,280 px / 128 MB (996x524) and pre-sizing ElementGL before upload() removed text stem pixelation; Chrome 159 on Android stays not verified.
